paragraphs.title: Israel Arrives at the Wilderness of Sinai

easy.question: In which month did the Israelites arrive at the wilderness of Sinai?
answers: The third month
The first month
The seventh month
easy.explanation: The verse says, “In the third month.”

easy.question: From which land did the Israelites leave?
answers: The land of Canaan
The land of Egypt
The land of Sinai
easy.explanation: The Israelites left the land of Egypt.

easy.question: Where did the Israelites camp?
answers: Beside the sea
Inside Egypt
Before the mountain
easy.explanation: The verse says that they camped in the wilderness before the mountain.

medium.question: What was the order of events according to the verses?
answers: They left Rephidim, came to Sinai, and camped there
They camped at Sinai, traveled to Rephidim, and returned to Egypt
They came to Egypt, traveled to Sinai, and returned to Rephidim
medium.explanation: First they left Rephidim, then came to the wilderness of Sinai, and finally camped there.

medium.question: What does “had pitched in the wilderness” mean in this context?
answers: They fought
They stopped and camped
They left quickly
medium.explanation: After traveling and arriving, they stopped and camped there.

medium.question: Why can we say that the Israelites arrived at a particular place rather than merely passing through?
answers: Because they camped there before the mountain
Because they immediately returned to Egypt
Because they remained at Rephidim
medium.explanation: The text says that they camped in the wilderness of Sinai, showing that they stopped there.

challenge.question: Which detail in the verses emphasizes the connection between the journey and the camping?
answers: The mention of the third month alone
The transition from “they left” to “they camped”
The mention of the land of Egypt alone
challenge.explanation: The verbs describe a sequence: first they left Rephidim, and afterward they camped in the wilderness of Sinai.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “before the mountain”?
answers: The camp was established in front of a particular mountain
The people climbed the mountain
The mountain was in Egypt
challenge.explanation: The phrase identifies the camp’s location: in front of the mountain, not on it.

challenge.question: What easily overlooked detail appears in the first verse?
answers: They arrived at Sinai on a particular day called “the same day”
The Israelites left Sinai before arriving there
The people first camped at Rephidim before the mountain
challenge.explanation: The verse specifically mentions the day of their arrival: “the same day came they into the wilderness of Sinai.”

questions.question: Which detail in the verses emphasizes the connection between the journey and the camping?
answers: The mention of the third month alone
The transition from “they left” to “they camped”
The mention of the land of Egypt alone
questions.explanation: The verbs describe a sequence: first they left Rephidim, and afterward they camped in the wilderness of Sinai.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “before the mountain”?
answers: The camp was established in front of a particular mountain
The people climbed the mountain
The mountain was in Egypt
questions.explanation: The phrase identifies the camp’s location: in front of the mountain, not on it.

questions.question: What easily overlooked detail appears in the first verse?
answers: They arrived at Sinai on a particular day called “the same day”
The Israelites left Sinai before arriving there
The people first camped at Rephidim before the mountain
questions.explanation: The verse specifically mentions the day of their arrival: “the same day came they into the wilderness of Sinai.”

paragraphs.title: The Covenant Offer and Israel’s Calling

easy.question: Who went up to God at the beginning of the passage?
answers: Moses
Pharaoh
Aaron
easy.explanation: The verse begins, “And Moses went up unto God.”

easy.question: How does the LORD describe what he did for the Israelites?
answers: He returned them to Egypt
He carried them on eagles’ wings
He hid them in the mountain
easy.explanation: The LORD says, “I bare you on eagles’ wings, and brought you unto myself.”

easy.question: What must the Israelites do to become the LORD’s treasured possession?
answers: Build a new city
Leave the land
Obey the LORD’s voice and keep his covenant
easy.explanation: The LORD gives this condition: “If ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant.”

medium.question: What is the order of events in the LORD’s words?
answers: The LORD acted against Egypt, carried Israel, and brought them to himself
Israel obeyed the LORD, and then he brought them out of Egypt
Israel became a kingdom of priests, and then Moses went up the mountain
medium.explanation: The passage first describes what the LORD did in Egypt, then how he carried Israel, and finally how he brought them to himself.

medium.question: What does “a peculiar treasure” mean in the phrase “a peculiar treasure unto me above all people”?
answers: A punishment
A valuable and special possession
A long journey
medium.explanation: The phrase means something valuable and special. “Above all people” shows that Israel would be specially treasured by the LORD.

medium.question: Why does the verse say, “for all the earth is mine,” after promising that Israel would be a treasured possession?
answers: To say that only Israel belongs to the LORD
To announce that all nations will leave the earth
To emphasize that the LORD owns the whole world yet chooses Israel as a special people
medium.explanation: The verse stresses that the whole earth belongs to the LORD, making his choice of Israel especially significant.

challenge.question: What is the central idea of the image “I bare you on eagles’ wings”?
answers: The LORD protected Israel and led them safely
The Israelites became eagles
Israel crossed the sea with the help of birds
challenge.explanation: The image describes the LORD’s protection and the way he brought Israel from Egypt to himself.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the names “house of Jacob” and “children of Israel” being used in the same passage?
answers: They are two different peoples
They are the same people known by two names
Only Jacob’s sons had to hear the message
challenge.explanation: “House of Jacob” and “children of Israel” are two names for the same people, so Moses was to deliver the message to all Israel.

challenge.question: What practical meaning does “a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation” have?
answers: The Israelites would be allowed to rule all nations
The Israelites would not need to keep commandments
The Israelites would have a special spiritual role and be committed to holiness
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes a special status and spiritual role, together with a requirement to live in holiness and keep the covenant.

questions.question: What is the central idea of the image “I bare you on eagles’ wings”?
answers: The LORD protected Israel and led them safely
The Israelites became eagles
Israel crossed the sea with the help of birds
questions.explanation: The image describes the LORD’s protection and the way he brought Israel from Egypt to himself.

questions.question: What can we understand from the names “house of Jacob” and “children of Israel” being used in the same passage?
answers: They are two different peoples
They are the same people known by two names
Only Jacob’s sons had to hear the message
questions.explanation: “House of Jacob” and “children of Israel” are two names for the same people, so Moses was to deliver the message to all Israel.

questions.question: What practical meaning does “a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation” have?
answers: The Israelites would be allowed to rule all nations
The Israelites would not need to keep commandments
The Israelites would have a special spiritual role and be committed to holiness
questions.explanation: The phrase describes a special status and spiritual role, together with a requirement to live in holiness and keep the covenant.

paragraphs.title: The People Accept the Covenant Words

easy.question: Whom did Moses call?
answers: The elders of the people
Pharaoh
The priests alone
easy.explanation: The verse says that Moses called the elders of the people.

easy.question: What did the people say in response to the LORD’s words?
answers: We will do nothing
All that the LORD has spoken we will do
We will wait for Moses
easy.explanation: The people declared that they would do everything the LORD had spoken.

easy.question: What did the LORD promise that the people would hear?
answers: Moses’ voice alone
The song of the angels
The LORD speaking with Moses
easy.explanation: The LORD said that the people would hear him speaking with Moses.

medium.question: What did Moses do after the people gave their answer?
answers: He went up the mountain alone
He brought the people’s words back to the LORD
He asked the people to repeat their words
medium.explanation: After the people answered, Moses reported their words to the LORD.

medium.question: Why would the LORD come to Moses in a thick cloud?
answers: To hide Moses from the people
To keep the people away from the mountain
So the people could hear the LORD speaking with Moses and believe in him
medium.explanation: The LORD explains that the people would hear him and thereby continue to believe in Moses.

medium.question: What does “together” mean in the phrase “all the people answered together”?
answers: Everyone at the same time
Each person separately
Only the elders
medium.explanation: “Together” means all at the same time; the entire people answered as one.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Moses reporting the people’s words to the LORD and then reporting them again?
answers: The people rejected the LORD’s words
Moses forgot what the people said
Moses served as an intermediary between the LORD and the people
challenge.explanation: The repeated reporting emphasizes Moses’ role as the link between the LORD and the people.

challenge.question: What was the main purpose of the people hearing the LORD speak with Moses?
answers: To strengthen the people’s faith in Moses
To teach the people the elders’ names
To announce that the people did not need to listen to Moses
challenge.explanation: The LORD says that the people would hear so that they would believe in Moses permanently.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the revelation was intended for the people as well as for Moses?
answers: Moses called the elders of the people
The people would hear the LORD speaking with Moses
Moses placed the words before the elders
challenge.explanation: The statement that the people would hear shows that they themselves were involved in the revelation.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Moses reporting the people’s words to the LORD and then reporting them again?
answers: The people rejected the LORD’s words
Moses forgot what the people said
Moses served as an intermediary between the LORD and the people
questions.explanation: The repeated reporting emphasizes Moses’ role as the link between the LORD and the people.

questions.question: What was the main purpose of the people hearing the LORD speak with Moses?
answers: To strengthen the people’s faith in Moses
To teach the people the elders’ names
To announce that the people did not need to listen to Moses
questions.explanation: The LORD says that the people would hear so that they would believe in Moses permanently.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the revelation was intended for the people as well as for Moses?
answers: Moses called the elders of the people
The people would hear the LORD speaking with Moses
Moses placed the words before the elders
questions.explanation: The statement that the people would hear shows that they themselves were involved in the revelation.

paragraphs.title: Preparing the People and Setting Boundaries Around the Mountain

easy.question: To whom did the LORD say, “Go unto the people”?
answers: Moses
Aaron
Pharaoh
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And the LORD said unto Moses, Go unto the people.”

easy.question: What were the people commanded to do with their clothes?
answers: Burn them
Wash them
Give them to the priests
easy.explanation: The people were commanded to wash their clothes in preparation for the third day.

easy.question: On which mountain would the LORD descend in the sight of all the people?
answers: Mount Carmel
Mount Zion
Mount Sinai
easy.explanation: The verse says that the LORD would descend in the sight of all the people upon Mount Sinai.

medium.question: Why were the people told to prepare for two days?
answers: Because the LORD would come down on Mount Sinai on the third day
Because they were leaving immediately
Because it was harvest time
medium.explanation: The preparations were for the third day, when the LORD would descend upon the mountain.

medium.question: What does “be ready” mean in the phrase “be ready against the third day”?
answers: Be tired
Be prepared
Be far away
medium.explanation: “Be ready” means be prepared for the LORD’s revelation on the third day.

medium.question: What was Moses to do around the people?
answers: Build them houses
Distribute food to them
Set bounds around the mountain
medium.explanation: Moses was commanded to set boundaries around the mountain so that no one would go up or touch its border.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the LORD descending on the mountain “in the sight of all the people”?
answers: The revelation was public, not secret
Only Moses saw the LORD
The people did not need to prepare
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the entire people witnessed the event, not Moses alone.

challenge.question: What condition was given for the people to come up to the mountain?
answers: The people had only to wash their clothes
The trumpet had to sound for a long time
Moses had to touch the border of the mountain
challenge.explanation: The text says that they could come up only when the trumpet sounded for a long time.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes the seriousness of the prohibition against approaching the mountain?
answers: The prohibition applied only to people
It was permitted to touch the border
The prohibition applied to both animals and people
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly mentions both beast and man, so the prohibition and punishment applied to animals and people.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the LORD descending on the mountain “in the sight of all the people”?
answers: The revelation was public, not secret
Only Moses saw the LORD
The people did not need to prepare
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the entire people witnessed the event, not Moses alone.

questions.question: What condition was given for the people to come up to the mountain?
answers: The people had only to wash their clothes
The trumpet had to sound for a long time
Moses had to touch the border of the mountain
questions.explanation: The text says that they could come up only when the trumpet sounded for a long time.

questions.question: Which detail emphasizes the seriousness of the prohibition against approaching the mountain?
answers: The prohibition applied only to people
It was permitted to touch the border
The prohibition applied to both animals and people
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly mentions both beast and man, so the prohibition and punishment applied to animals and people.

paragraphs.title: The People Consecrate Themselves and Wait

easy.question: Who came down from the mountain to the people?
answers: Moses
Aaron
Joshua
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And Moses went down from the mount unto the people.”

easy.question: What did the people wash?
answers: Their tents
Their clothes
Their shoes
easy.explanation: The verse says, “They washed their clothes.”

easy.question: What did Moses command the people to avoid?
answers: Eating bread
Sleeping at night
Coming near their wives
easy.explanation: Moses said, “Come not at your wives.”

medium.question: What did Moses do after coming down from the mountain to the people?
answers: He sent them home
He consecrated the people
He built them an altar
medium.explanation: After coming down, Moses consecrated the people.

medium.question: What does “be ready” mean in the phrase “Be ready against the third day”?
answers: Be tired
Be far away
Be prepared
medium.explanation: In the context of preparing for the third day, “be ready” means be prepared.

medium.question: How did the people prepare for the third day?
answers: By washing their clothes and abstaining from marital relations
By leaving the camp and preparing for a journey
By eating a feast and building tents
medium.explanation: Their preparation included washing their clothes and refraining from marital relations.

challenge.question: What can be learned from the change from singular to plural in “he consecrated the people, and they washed their clothes”?
answers: Moses consecrated the people, and the people washed their clothes
The whole people consecrated Moses
Moses washed the people’s clothes himself
challenge.explanation: The verbs show that Moses consecrated the people, while the people washed their own clothes.

challenge.question: What is the connection between “Be ready against the third day” and the other instructions?
answers: The instructions canceled the three days
They explain how to prepare during that time
They indicate that the people had to leave immediately
challenge.explanation: Washing their clothes and abstaining from marital relations were preparations for the third day.

challenge.question: What does “Come not at your wives” mean in the verse?
answers: Do not speak with women
Do not stand near women
Abstain from marital relations
challenge.explanation: The phrase is a respectful reference to intimacy between husband and wife, so it means to abstain from marital relations.

questions.question: What can be learned from the change from singular to plural in “he consecrated the people, and they washed their clothes”?
answers: Moses consecrated the people, and the people washed their clothes
The whole people consecrated Moses
Moses washed the people’s clothes himself
questions.explanation: The verbs show that Moses consecrated the people, while the people washed their own clothes.

questions.question: What is the connection between “Be ready against the third day” and the other instructions?
answers: The instructions canceled the three days
They explain how to prepare during that time
They indicate that the people had to leave immediately
questions.explanation: Washing their clothes and abstaining from marital relations were preparations for the third day.

questions.question: What does “Come not at your wives” mean in the verse?
answers: Do not speak with women
Do not stand near women
Abstain from marital relations
questions.explanation: The phrase is a respectful reference to intimacy between husband and wife, so it means to abstain from marital relations.

paragraphs.title: The LORD Appears on Mount Sinai

easy.question: When did the events in these verses take place?
answers: On the third day in the morning
On the first evening
At noon on the seventh day
easy.explanation: The verse begins, “On the third day in the morning.”

easy.question: How did the people in the camp react to the thunder, lightning, and cloud?
answers: They rejoiced
They trembled and were afraid
They returned to Egypt
easy.explanation: The verse says that all the people in the camp trembled.

easy.question: Where did the Israelites stand after Moses brought them out of the camp?
answers: At the top of the mountain
Inside the fire
At the foot of the mountain
easy.explanation: The verse says that they stood at the lower part of the mountain.

medium.question: What did Moses do after the people trembled in the camp?
answers: He brought the people out of the camp to meet God
He sent the people back to their tents
He went up to the top of the mountain alone
medium.explanation: Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet God.

medium.question: What does “the lower part” mean in the phrase “they stood at the lower part of the mountain”?
answers: The summit
The foot or base of the mountain
The side farthest from the mountain
medium.explanation: It means the lowest part, showing that the people stood at the base rather than at the top.

medium.question: Why was Mount Sinai completely covered with smoke?
answers: Because the people lit fires
Because there was a storm in the camp
Because the LORD descended upon it in fire
medium.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the mountain smoked because the LORD descended upon it in fire.

challenge.question: What happened before the Israelites stood at the foot of the mountain?
answers: Moses brought them out of the camp to meet God
The mountain became smoky like a furnace
The people climbed to the top
challenge.explanation: According to the order of the verses, Moses first brought the people out of the camp, and then they stood at the foot of the mountain.

challenge.question: What is the exact difference between the trembling in verse 16 and the trembling in verse 18?
answers: Only Moses trembled in both verses
The people trembled in verse 16, and the mountain trembled in verse 18
The mountain trembled in verse 16, and the people trembled in verse 18
challenge.explanation: Verse 16 says that all the people trembled, while verse 18 says that the whole mountain quaked.

challenge.question: What does the comparison “as the smoke of a furnace” emphasize about Sinai’s smoke?
answers: The smoke came from a house
The smoke was cold and invisible
The smoke was thick and clearly visible
challenge.explanation: The comparison creates an image of abundant, thick, and highly visible smoke.

questions.question: What happened before the Israelites stood at the foot of the mountain?
answers: Moses brought them out of the camp to meet God
The mountain became smoky like a furnace
The people climbed to the top
questions.explanation: According to the order of the verses, Moses first brought the people out of the camp, and then they stood at the foot of the mountain.

questions.question: What is the exact difference between the trembling in verse 16 and the trembling in verse 18?
answers: Only Moses trembled in both verses
The people trembled in verse 16, and the mountain trembled in verse 18
The mountain trembled in verse 16, and the people trembled in verse 18
questions.explanation: Verse 16 says that all the people trembled, while verse 18 says that the whole mountain quaked.

questions.question: What does the comparison “as the smoke of a furnace” emphasize about Sinai’s smoke?
answers: The smoke came from a house
The smoke was cold and invisible
The smoke was thick and clearly visible
questions.explanation: The comparison creates an image of abundant, thick, and highly visible smoke.

paragraphs.title: The Trumpet’s Sound and Moses Goes Up the Mountain

easy.question: What happened to the sound of the trumpet?
answers: It grew weaker
It grew louder and louder
It stopped immediately
easy.explanation: The verse says that it grew louder and louder.

easy.question: Who spoke in the passage?
answers: Moses
Aaron
Pharaoh
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “Moses spake.”

easy.question: What did Moses do after the LORD called him to the top of the mountain?
answers: He went down
He hid
He went up
easy.explanation: The verse ends by saying, “Moses went up.”

medium.question: What happened after Moses spoke?
answers: The mountain disappeared
God answered him by a voice
The trumpet became silent
medium.explanation: The verse says that Moses spoke and God answered him by a voice.

medium.question: What does “answered him” mean in the phrase “God answered him by a voice”?
answers: God replied to him
God taught him
God sent him away
medium.explanation: The phrase means that God replied to Moses; Moses spoke and God responded by voice.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events according to the verses?
answers: Moses went up, the LORD called him, and then the trumpet grew louder
The LORD descended, Moses went up, and then Moses spoke
The trumpet grew louder, Moses spoke, God answered and called Moses, and Moses went up
medium.explanation: This is the order described: the trumpet grew louder, Moses spoke, God answered, called Moses, and Moses went up.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the LORD answering Moses by voice and also calling him?
answers: There was direct communication between the LORD and Moses
Moses was not allowed to approach the mountain
The trumpet spoke instead of Moses
challenge.explanation: The LORD responds to Moses and calls him, showing direct communication between them.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes the location from which the LORD called Moses?
answers: The words “by a voice”
The repeated phrase “to the top of the mountain”
The word “trumpet”
challenge.explanation: The phrase “to the top of the mountain” identifies the place of the revelation and meeting.

challenge.question: What is special about the movements of the LORD and Moses in verse 20?
answers: They both went down the mountain
Moses went down and the LORD went up
The LORD came down to the mountain, and Moses went up to him
challenge.explanation: The verse says that the LORD descended upon Mount Sinai and, after calling Moses, Moses went up to the top.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the LORD answering Moses by voice and also calling him?
answers: There was direct communication between the LORD and Moses
Moses was not allowed to approach the mountain
The trumpet spoke instead of Moses
questions.explanation: The LORD responds to Moses and calls him, showing direct communication between them.

questions.question: Which detail emphasizes the location from which the LORD called Moses?
answers: The words “by a voice”
The repeated phrase “to the top of the mountain”
The word “trumpet”
questions.explanation: The phrase “to the top of the mountain” identifies the place of the revelation and meeting.

questions.question: What is special about the movements of the LORD and Moses in verse 20?
answers: They both went down the mountain
Moses went down and the LORD went up
The LORD came down to the mountain, and Moses went up to him
questions.explanation: The verse says that the LORD descended upon Mount Sinai and, after calling Moses, Moses went up to the top.

easy.question: Who commanded Moses to go down and warn the people?
answers: The LORD
Aaron
The priests
easy.explanation: The LORD says to Moses, “Go down, charge the people.”

easy.question: What might happen to those who went up the mountain to gaze at the LORD?
answers: They would remain there
Many of them would perish
They would become priests
easy.explanation: The verse warns that many of them would perish.

easy.question: Who went down to the people at the end of the passage?
answers: Aaron
The priests
Moses
easy.explanation: The final verse says, “So Moses went down unto the people.”

medium.question: Why did Moses say that the people could not come up Mount Sinai?
answers: Because the LORD had commanded that the mountain be bounded and consecrated
Because Moses did not know the way
Because Aaron forbade the people to go up
medium.explanation: Moses recalled that the LORD had commanded, “Set bounds about the mount, and sanctify it.”

medium.question: What does “break through unto the LORD to gaze” mean?
answers: Sing to the LORD
Break through the boundary and approach the LORD without permission
Build an altar to the LORD
medium.explanation: The context concerns people trying to go up the mountain to see the LORD, so it means breaking through the boundary without permission.

medium.question: Who was permitted to go up the mountain with Moses?
answers: All the people
All the priests
Aaron
medium.explanation: The LORD says, “Thou shalt come up, thou, and Aaron with thee,” while forbidding the priests and people to come up.

challenge.question: What distinction is made between the groups mentioned in the LORD’s command?
answers: Moses and Aaron may go up, but the priests and people may not
The people may go up, while only Moses must remain below
The priests may go up, while Aaron remains with the people
challenge.explanation: The command distinguishes Moses and Aaron, who may go up, from the priests and people, who may not approach.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the fact that even the priests had to sanctify themselves?
answers: The priests had no connection with worship
Even those close to the LORD’s service must observe holiness and boundaries
The priests were allowed to go up without restriction
challenge.explanation: The verse specifically mentions the priests who come near the LORD, yet still commands them to sanctify themselves and respect the boundary.

challenge.question: What does the sequence “Go down” followed by “thou shalt come up” emphasize?
answers: Moses was confused about which direction to go
The people had to go up before Moses
Moses had to go down to warn the people and afterward go up with Aaron
challenge.explanation: The LORD tells Moses to go down and warn the people, then clarifies that he may go up only with Aaron.

questions.question: What distinction is made between the groups mentioned in the LORD’s command?
answers: Moses and Aaron may go up, but the priests and people may not
The people may go up, while only Moses must remain below
The priests may go up, while Aaron remains with the people
questions.explanation: The command distinguishes Moses and Aaron, who may go up, from the priests and people, who may not approach.

questions.question: What can we understand from the fact that even the priests had to sanctify themselves?
answers: The priests had no connection with worship
Even those close to the LORD’s service must observe holiness and boundaries
The priests were allowed to go up without restriction
questions.explanation: The verse specifically mentions the priests who come near the LORD, yet still commands them to sanctify themselves and respect the boundary.

questions.question: What does the sequence “Go down” followed by “thou shalt come up” emphasize?
answers: Moses was confused about which direction to go
The people had to go up before Moses
Moses had to go down to warn the people and afterward go up with Aaron
questions.explanation: The LORD tells Moses to go down and warn the people, then clarifies that he may go up only with Aaron.
